doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: White musicians in that scene and Gato Barbieri's band
summary: Joe Beck was in his first group at Thiele's wish; Stanley Clarke and Airto left Gato to form Return to Forever.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I’m about to wrap up here, but when I look at the recordings of that time, Pharoah Sanders’ time and into the 70s, it doesn’t look like there was a lot of white musicians, if any, that sort of participated in that style of music. In fact I think you had Joe Beck in your first group?

Oh yeah, well Bob — Bob wanted Joe in because Joe did some recordings. Because I remember the record, oh shoot, that’s another story. When Gato — we were on the road one time, we had Stanley Clarke on bass and Airto was playing drums. So we were in Philadelphia and the last night of the engagement in Philadelphia Stanley and Airto told Gato, he said, “Well we’ll see you — we’re getting ready to go to California.” So we said what’s happening? They were going to California to form their group Return to Forever with Chick Corea. And so you know but that’s a good point. I don’t remember any — no, because Monk, we were creating. Because when you’re really creating you don’t know what’s coming next. So I don’t remember any of them, they came in later I think. But now, that’s one thing that kind of upsets me about Sirius FM, you know, now it’s the complete opposite.
